messages:
Ravi (Customer): Hey team — seeing intermittent 429s and weird quota headers. Customer says some requests get `x-rate-limit-remaining` and others don't. Happens across two API keys and two different machines (different public IPs). Can we confirm how limits are scoped? org vs project vs key vs IP?

Maya (Support): Thanks for the report, Ravi. Can you paste the raw response headers and the curl you're using? Also curious whether the requests that succeed vs fail are identical (same endpoint, same payload size). :thinking:

Ravi (Customer): Minimal repro below. Same payload, same endpoint `/v1/generate`. One request returns 200 + headers, next returns 429 with no x-rate-limit headers.

```
# OK
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ABC" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 200 OK
x-rate-limit-limit: 120
x-rate-limit-remaining: 57
x-rate-limit-reset: 1670000000
\n# Failing
curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk-prod-ABC" -d '{"prompt":"hi"}' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
HTTP/1.1 429 Too Many Requests
content-type: application/json
{"error":"rate limit exceeded"}
```

Ravi (Customer): Keys: `sk-prod-ABC` (project-scoped), and `sk-org-XYZ` (org master key). Both show mixed behavior. The machines are on different NAT IPs: 34.67.1.9 and 34.67.1.10.

Maya (Support): Ok. Quick checklist: 1) send full request ids from response body if present, 2) include server timestamps, 3) confirm whether same API key + different IPs reproduce.

Leo (SRE): FYI we have layered rate limits: per-key (short window burst), per-project (sustained), per-org (overall committed), and a soft IP-based anti-abuse throttle for anonymous keys or unusual traffic patterns. However, `x-rate-limit-*` headers are only emitted when the request is accepted by the rate limiter service instance that sees/handles the traffic; in rare races they can be missing for 429s generated by the global throttle layer.

Nadia (Eng): Adding details — there are two enforcement points: edge-proxy (fast, local, IP/token checks) and global quota service (stronger, eventual consistency). Edge tries to attach `x-rate-limit-*` from local counters; if the global service returns deny after edge forwarded, the response may not include those headers. That's likely why 429 sometimes lacks headers.

Ravi (Customer): That matches timing — failures are bursty after a deploy and then calm. Is there a way to force getting headers even on global-deny? We need to show customers the limit remaining.

Maya (Support): Short-term workaround: rotate to a project-specific key and avoid using the org master key for high QPS; project keys get consistent header emission. Also can route traffic through the same egress IP (e.g., via NAT) to avoid IP-based soft throttles.

Leo (SRE): Repro steps I just ran from two egress IPs (local office + CI runner). Steps: 1) issue 200 requests/s for ~30s with `sk-prod-ABC` from IP A; 2) switch to IP B and continue at 50r/s. Observed: edge allowed bursts, global service applied an org-level cap and returned 429s without headers. I captured request-ids: `req_3a9f`, `req_3a9f+1` etc.

Nadia (Eng): To be explicit about scoping: - API key: enforces per-key short-window burst limits (token bucket) and provides headers. - Project: enforces sustained throughput per project across keys. - Org: hard cap if customer has reserved capacity; for trial accounts it's a lower global cap. - IP: soft block for unusual patterns and for unauthenticated/guest usage.

Ravi (Customer): Is the billing meter tied to org or project? Because our billing spikes don't match the org quota shown in the console.

Maya (Support): Billing is billed at the org level (aggregation). Usage visibility in Console offers both project and org views; the meter that affects bills is org. If org use exceeds reserved Dedicated, you may hit org-level throttles.

Ravi (Customer): Ok — customer is on free-tier, but they claimed they were within per-key limits. They were using the org master key from several services and a CI job that did retries. Maybe retries + many IPs caused org cap.

Leo (SRE): Action items from SRE: 1) look up org id `org_0xy` and share recent windows (15m/1h) of enforcement events, include request ids; 2) correlate IPs -> we saw ~8 distinct egress IPs from that org in last 24h.

Nadia (Eng): Also adding a small code snippet for deterministic repro (single-threaded to avoid client-side retry storms):

```
# python repro
import requests
for i in range(300):
    r = requests.post('https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate', headers={'Authorization':'Bearer sk-prod-ABC'}, json={'prompt':'x'})
    print(i, r.status_code, r.headers.get('x-rate-limit-remaining'))
```

Maya (Support): For now I'm going to: 1) notify billing if we need to temporarily raise org cap (customer approval required), 2) recommend rotating to a project key & consolidating egress IPs, 3) provide repro snippet to customer. Ravi — want me to ask for temporary org bump? :wave:

Ravi (Customer): Yes please, requesting a short bump during their upcoming marketing send. Also please include the list of offending IPs and the exact time windows so customer can reconcile with their outbound logs.

Leo (SRE): I'm pulling logs now. Found a pattern: CI runners did exponential-backoff but with very low jitter so many retries aligned, causing bursts at the edge. Recommend adding randomized jitter to backoff. Also we'll attach the raw request-ids to the support ticket.

Nadia (Eng): Long-term notes for product: make `x-rate-limit-*` emitted on all 429s (global denies) and add header that indicates which scope caused the deny (e.g., `x-rate-limit-scope: org|project|key|ip`) — filing internal ticket.

Maya (Support): Escalation plan: (a) SRE to provide IP list & request ids (ETA 30m), (b) billing to consider temporary bump (pending customer approval), (c) Eng to file header-improvement ticket. I'll update ticket #SUP-4287 with artifacts. :white_check_mark:

billing-bot: Billing notification: review request SUP-4287 for temporary quota increase — please confirm PO or approval from account.

Ravi (Customer): Thanks, team. Will share approval and ask infra to consolidate outbound IPs and add jitter to retries. Will follow up once we have the bump.

Maya (Support): Closing loop: once SRE posts IPs and windows I'll attach to ticket and schedule a short post-mortem to summarize root cause & remed. Thanks everyone. :pray:
